areas.name: Algebra
areas.description: Equations, polynomials, functions, sequences and inequalities: turning words into symbols and then moving the symbols around with purpose.

areas.name: Geometry
areas.description: Angles, triangles, circles, areas, coordinates and solids: finding the hidden right triangle or similar pair that makes a length or an area fall out.

areas.name: Number theory
areas.description: Divisibility, primes, remainders, digits and integer equations: questions that only make sense because the answers must be whole numbers.

areas.name: Counting and probability
areas.description: Arrangements, selections, distributions, probability and expected value: counting things without listing them and without counting any twice.

topics.name: Linear equations and word problems
topics.description: Setting up and solving linear equations and systems from a story: rates, work, mixtures, ages and distance-speed-time.

topics.name: Ratios, percents and averages
topics.description: Percent change, successive percents, ratios that combine, and means that shift when a value is added or removed.

topics.name: Quadratics
topics.description: Factoring, completing the square, the quadratic formula, the discriminant and the vertex of a parabola.

topics.name: Polynomials and their roots
topics.description: Relationships between coefficients and roots, the remainder and factor theorems, and evaluating a polynomial at a well-chosen point.

topics.name: Exponents and radicals
topics.description: Laws of exponents, rewriting powers in a common base, simplifying and rationalizing radicals, and nested roots.

topics.name: Logarithms
topics.description: Log laws, change of base, and equations where the unknown sits in an exponent or inside a logarithm.

topics.name: Sequences and series
topics.description: Arithmetic and geometric sequences and their sums, recursively defined sequences, and sums that collapse.

topics.name: Functions and functional equations
topics.description: Composition, inverses, graphs and transformations of functions, and equations whose unknown is a function.

topics.name: Inequalities and optimization
topics.description: Finding a largest or smallest value with AM-GM, squares being nonnegative, or a vertex, and proving the bound is reached.

topics.name: Complex numbers
topics.description: Arithmetic in rectangular and polar form, modulus and argument, conjugates, De Moivre's theorem and roots of unity.

topics.name: Absolute value, floor and piecewise
topics.description: Equations and graphs with absolute values, the floor and ceiling functions, and functions defined in pieces.

topics.name: Angles and polygons
topics.description: Parallel lines, interior and exterior angles of polygons, regular polygons and angle relationships in a figure.

topics.name: Similar and congruent triangles
topics.description: Spotting similar triangles, setting up proportions, and using congruence to move lengths and angles around a figure.

topics.name: Right triangles and the Pythagorean theorem
topics.description: Pythagorean triples, 30-60-90 and 45-45-90 triangles, and building a right triangle where none is drawn.

topics.name: Area and perimeter
topics.description: Areas of triangles, quadrilaterals and composite regions, Heron's formula, and comparing areas through shared heights or bases.

topics.name: Circles
topics.description: Arcs, chords, tangents, inscribed angles, power of a point and cyclic quadrilaterals.

topics.name: Coordinate geometry
topics.description: Lines, slopes, distances, midpoints and areas in the coordinate plane, including the shoelace formula.

topics.name: Three-dimensional geometry
topics.description: Volume and surface area of prisms, cylinders, cones, spheres and pyramids, and distances inside a solid.

topics.name: Triangle centers and special lengths
topics.description: Inradius, circumradius, medians, altitudes, the angle bisector theorem and the centers they meet at.

topics.name: Trigonometry
topics.description: Sine, cosine and tangent, the law of sines and the law of cosines, identities, and trig equations.

topics.name: Transformations and symmetry
topics.description: Reflections, rotations, dilations and the symmetries of a figure, used to shorten a path or match up equal parts.

topics.name: Conic sections
topics.description: Parabolas, ellipses and hyperbolas from their equations: foci, axes and the geometry they encode.

topics.name: Divisibility
topics.description: Divisibility rules, what it means for one integer to divide another, and divisibility of expressions in n.

topics.name: Primes and prime factorization
topics.description: Recognizing primes, factoring into primes, and reading properties of a number off its factorization.

topics.name: Divisors
topics.description: Counting divisors, summing them, pairing them up, and divisors with an extra condition such as being a perfect square.

topics.name: GCD and LCM
topics.description: Greatest common divisors and least common multiples, the identity linking them, and the Euclidean algorithm.

topics.name: Modular arithmetic
topics.description: Remainders, congruences, cycles of last digits, and Fermat's little theorem for powers modulo a prime.

topics.name: Digits and bases
topics.description: Digit sums, place value, writing numbers in other bases and problems about the digits of a number.

topics.name: Integer equations
topics.description: Equations that must be solved in integers: linear Diophantine equations, factoring tricks and bounding.

topics.name: Factorials and prime powers
topics.description: The exponent of a prime in a factorial, trailing zeros, and the largest power of a prime dividing a product.

topics.name: Parity and integer properties
topics.description: Odd and even arguments, perfect squares and cubes, and properties that force or rule out an integer answer.

topics.name: Fractions and decimals
topics.description: Repeating and terminating decimals, fractions in lowest terms, and converting between the two.

topics.name: Counting principles
topics.description: The multiplication and addition principles, and organizing a count so every case is counted once.

topics.name: Permutations and arrangements
topics.description: Ordered arrangements, arrangements with repeated letters, circular arrangements and arrangements with restrictions.

topics.name: Combinations and binomial coefficients
topics.description: Choosing subsets, Pascal's triangle, the binomial theorem and identities between binomial coefficients.

topics.name: Inclusion-exclusion and complements
topics.description: Counting a union by adding and subtracting overlaps, and counting what you do not want and subtracting.

topics.name: Distributions
topics.description: Putting identical or distinct objects into boxes, with or without empty boxes, including stars and bars.

topics.name: Probability
topics.description: Equally likely outcomes, independent events, and probabilities built from counts of favourable and total cases.

topics.name: Conditional and geometric probability
topics.description: Probability given that something happened, and probability measured as a length, area or volume ratio.

topics.name: Expected value
topics.description: Averages over random outcomes, linearity of expectation and expected waiting times.

topics.name: Recursion and states
topics.description: Counting or probability problems solved by relating the answer for n to the answers for smaller cases.

topics.name: Paths and grids
topics.description: Lattice paths, paths that avoid or must pass through points, and counting figures such as rectangles on a grid.

topics.name: Combinatorial reasoning
topics.description: Pigeonhole, invariants, games and logic puzzles where the answer comes from an argument rather than a formula.

types.name: Complementary counting
types.description: Count the outcomes you do not want, which is often far easier, and subtract from the total.
recognizeWhen: The question says at least one, or not all
The wanted cases split into many messy subcases
The unwanted case is a single clean condition
A probability asks for something to happen at least once

types.name: Casework
types.description: Split the problem into a few cases that do not overlap and together cover everything, then handle each case on its own.
recognizeWhen: One choice changes which rules apply to the rest
A variable can be positive, zero or negative and each behaves differently
The count depends on a first digit, a first move or a largest part
No single formula covers all the possibilities

types.name: Stars and bars
types.description: Count the ways to split identical objects among distinct boxes by arranging objects and dividers in a row.
recognizeWhen: Identical items go to distinct people or boxes
The question counts nonnegative or positive integer solutions of a sum
Order within a box does not matter
A minimum per box can be handed out first

types.name: Telescoping
types.description: Rewrite each term as a difference so that neighbouring terms cancel and only the first and last pieces survive.
recognizeWhen: A long sum of fractions with products in the denominator
A long product of fractions where numerators match later denominators
Terms of the form 1 over n times n plus k
Square roots of consecutive integers appear in denominators

types.name: Vieta's formulas
types.description: Read sums and products of the roots straight off the coefficients instead of finding the roots themselves.
recognizeWhen: A symmetric expression in the roots of a given polynomial
The roots are ugly or complex but their sum or product is wanted
You are told two roots and asked for a coefficient
Sum of squares or reciprocals of the roots

types.name: Clever factoring (SFFT)
types.description: Add a constant to both sides so that an expression like xy plus ax plus by factors as a product, then list factor pairs.
recognizeWhen: An equation in integers mixes a product xy with linear terms
Reciprocal equations such as 1/x plus 1/y equals a constant
The question counts integer or positive integer solutions
Cross-multiplying leaves xy on one side

types.name: Invariants
types.description: Find a quantity that a repeated move never changes, such as a parity or a sum modulo some number, and use it to rule outcomes in or out.
recognizeWhen: A process repeats a move many times
The question asks whether a final state is possible
Numbers are replaced by their sum, difference or product
Coins, lights or chips are flipped in groups

types.name: Pigeonhole principle
types.description: If more objects go into fewer boxes than there are objects, some box holds at least two, which guarantees a coincidence.
recognizeWhen: The question asks for the minimum needed to guarantee something
Worst-case wording such as no matter how they are chosen
Remainders, colours or birthdays must repeat
A count of objects just exceeds a count of categories

types.name: Modular arithmetic
types.description: Work only with remainders, replacing large numbers by small ones with the same remainder, to find units digits, remainders or impossibilities.
recognizeWhen: A remainder or units digit of a huge power or product
An equation that must be checked for integer solutions
Something repeats in a cycle
Divisibility of an expression for every n

types.name: Power of a point
types.description: For two lines through a point meeting a circle, the products of the distances to the intersection points are equal.
recognizeWhen: Two chords cross inside a circle
Two secants, or a secant and a tangent, from an outside point
Lengths along lines through a circle with one unknown segment
A tangent length from a point outside a circle

types.name: Similar triangles
types.description: Find two triangles with matching angles and use the constant ratio of their sides to transfer a known length to an unknown one.
recognizeWhen: Parallel lines cut across a triangle
Two triangles share an angle and have another equal angle
An altitude is dropped to the hypotenuse of a right triangle
Shadows, mirrors or nested shapes

types.name: Coordinate bash
types.description: Place the figure on axes with convenient points at the origin and on the axes, then compute lengths and areas with algebra.
recognizeWhen: A square, rectangle or right angle gives natural axes
Midpoints and intersection points of lines are involved
Synthetic angle work is not getting anywhere
Distances from a moving point to fixed points

types.name: Mass points
types.description: Assign weights to vertices so that cevians balance, then read off ratios of segments without writing a single equation.
recognizeWhen: Two or more cevians of a triangle cross
Points divide sides in given ratios
The question asks for a ratio along a cevian
Ratios of segments rather than actual lengths

types.name: Angle chasing
types.description: Label one unknown angle and push it around the figure with triangle sums, parallel lines, isosceles triangles and inscribed angles.
recognizeWhen: The answer is an angle in degrees
Isosceles triangles or equal chords appear
Parallel lines and transversals
Points on a circle with an inscribed angle

types.name: Linearity of expectation
types.description: Write the quantity as a sum of simple indicator variables and add their expected values, even when the events depend on each other.
recognizeWhen: Expected number of something, such as fixed points or matches
The events overlap and are clearly not independent
Counting pairs or neighbours that share a property
A direct distribution of the total would be miserable

types.name: Recursion
types.description: Express the answer for size n in terms of answers for smaller sizes, compute the small cases, and build up.
recognizeWhen: Tilings, staircases or strings with no two adjacent of a kind
The answer for n clearly depends on the last step taken
A random walk or game with a few states
Small cases are easy but the asked size is large

types.name: Symmetry
types.description: Use a symmetry of the situation to pair up cases, swap roles, or argue that two quantities must be equal.
recognizeWhen: Two players, colours or outcomes are interchangeable
A probability of more heads than tails or similar
A figure is symmetric about a line or point
An expression is unchanged when variables are swapped

types.name: Working backwards
types.description: Start from the final state and undo each step, which is often deterministic even when going forward is not.
recognizeWhen: The end result of a process is given and the start is asked
Each step can be reversed uniquely
Repeated halving, doubling or giving away fractions
A game where the last position is easy to analyse

types.name: Extreme principle
types.description: Look at the largest, smallest, first or last object; its special position often forces the structure of everything else.
recognizeWhen: The question asks for the greatest or least possible value
A configuration of points, numbers or people with an ordering
Proving something cannot go on forever
Consider the largest number in a list with given sums

types.name: Bounding
types.description: Trap the answer between an upper and a lower bound, then check the few remaining candidates.
recognizeWhen: An integer answer with a huge apparent search space
Inequalities that squeeze a variable into a small range
Estimating a sum, root or power to the nearest integer
Showing a maximum is attained after proving it cannot be beaten

types.name: Inclusion-exclusion
types.description: Count a union by adding the sizes of the sets, subtracting the pairwise overlaps, adding back triple overlaps, and so on.
recognizeWhen: Divisible by at least one of several numbers
Overlapping groups such as students taking two subjects
Counting with an or between conditions
Arrangements where certain items must not be in certain places

types.name: Bijection
types.description: Match the objects being counted one-to-one with objects that are easier to count.
recognizeWhen: The count looks hard but resembles a known count
Each object is determined by a simpler choice
Paths, subsets or strings that encode one another
A substitution such as n equals 12k changes the question

types.name: Substitution
types.description: Replace a repeated expression with a single new variable, or shift a variable, so that the equation becomes familiar.
recognizeWhen: The same expression appears several times
An equation is quadratic in some power or root of x
A system becomes simple in sums and products of the variables
Shifting x by a constant removes a term

types.name: Small cases and patterns
types.description: Work out the answer for the first few sizes, spot the pattern, then justify it before using it for the asked size.
recognizeWhen: The question uses a large specific number like 2026
A process is repeated n times
The answer seems to depend on n in a regular way
Direct computation is impossible but n equals 1, 2, 3 is quick

types.name: Area ratios
types.description: Compare areas through shared heights or bases, or through the square of a similarity ratio, instead of computing each area.
recognizeWhen: A triangle is cut by segments from a vertex
The answer is a fraction of a whole area
Similar shapes nested inside each other
Points divide sides in given ratios and an area is asked

types.name: Auxiliary construction
types.description: Draw one extra segment, such as a radius to a tangent point or a perpendicular, to create a right triangle or a similar pair.
recognizeWhen: A tangent line touches a circle
Two circles touch or their centres are given
A trapezoid or irregular quadrilateral needs a height
The figure has no triangle that contains the unknown

types.name: Parity
types.description: Track whether quantities are odd or even to show a target is impossible or to cut the cases in half.
recognizeWhen: A sum or product must be odd or even
Moves that always change a count by two
Checkerboard colourings
An integer equation with odd and even terms

types.name: AM-GM
types.description: The arithmetic mean of nonnegative numbers is at least their geometric mean, with equality when they are all equal.
recognizeWhen: Minimize a sum whose product is fixed
Maximize a product whose sum is fixed
Expressions like x plus k over x for positive x
Equality looks likely when the variables are equal

types.name: Geometric probability
types.description: Model a random choice of real numbers as a point in a region and find the probability as a ratio of lengths or areas.
recognizeWhen: Two numbers are chosen at random from an interval
Someone arrives at a uniformly random time
A point is picked at random inside a shape
A condition becomes an inequality in two variables

types.name: Periodicity
types.description: Find the period of a repeating sequence, then reduce the large index modulo that period.
recognizeWhen: The 2026th term of a recursively defined sequence
Units digits of powers
A function applied to itself many times
Days of the week or positions around a circle

types.name: Prime factorization
types.description: Write each number as a product of prime powers and turn the question into one about exponents.
recognizeWhen: Divisors, multiples, squares or cubes of a given number
A product must be a perfect power
LCM or GCD conditions
Factorials or products of many integers

types.name: Evaluate at a clever point
types.description: Plug a special value such as 0, 1, -1 or i into a polynomial or identity so that most terms vanish or combine.
recognizeWhen: The sum of the coefficients of a polynomial
A product like (r + 1)(s + 1)(t + 1) over the roots
The remainder when a polynomial is divided by a linear factor
Alternating sums of binomial coefficients

types.name: Use the answer choices
types.description: Test the choices, eliminate the impossible ones by parity, size or units digit, or plug a choice back into the conditions.
recognizeWhen: The choices differ in an easily checked property
Solving forward is long but checking is fast
Only one choice has the right units digit or parity
An estimate already separates the choices

types.name: Roots of unity
types.description: Use the complex solutions of z to the n equals 1, their symmetry around the circle and their zero sum.
recognizeWhen: Powers of a complex number land on a regular polygon
Sums of every third or fourth binomial coefficient
z to the n equals 1 or a factor of it appears
Products over all nth roots of unity
